what: Guard patterns (`pat if guard`, rustc feature `guard_patterns`): the grammar gained `ast::Pat::GuardPat` but hir-def has no HIR pattern for it, so `crates/hir-def/src/expr_store/lower.rs` `collect_pat` lowers it to `Pat::Missing` (as it already does `ConstBlockPat`), which made the match exhaustive for the first compile. Needed for superset-of-rust: a `Pat::Guard { pat: PatId, guard: ExprId }` in `crates/hir-def/src/hir.rs` (+ columns/persist/pretty), lowered in `collect_pat` with the inner pattern bindings in scope of the guard, then inference in hir-ty and MIR building in hir-ty-mir (lane codegen) following rustc `guard_patterns` (rustc_mir_build matches.rs). Every exhaustive `match` on `Pat` in hir-ty, hir-ty-mir, hir-ty-matchck, blaze-diagnostics gains an arm, so it should land as one change across lanes.
why: format first: Pat::Guard goes in crates/hir-def/src/hir.rs and its columns/persist/pretty and collect_pat in expr_store/lower.rs, all format's files (crates.md). Once Pat::Guard exists, file the hir-ty inference arm to db and MIR building to codegen; db will add the hir-ty/matchck arms in the same change
